archetype.name: Dual-Threat (rookie-developmental)
archetype.definition: A second-year mobile starter whose legs carried his rookie production, and whose arm was cleaner in a tiny 2026 sample before he lost the job.

report.headline: One sharp game against the league's worst defense, now buried at QB4
report.take:
Dart's 2026 is really one game. Week 1 against Dallas, a defense that now ranks 32nd in EPA, he went 23 of 29 for 230 yards and three touchdowns and added 54 rushing yards on 11 carries. That is 230 of his 250 passing yards and all of his rushing. In Week 2 at the Rams he played 12% of the snaps and threw five passes, then missed practice in Week 3. Jameis Winston has started every game since, and the depth chart now lists Dart as QB4. The dossier doesn't say why he left the Rams game, so treat his role as the main story and the stat line as a footnote.

The Dallas game showed some real growth from his rookie profile. In 2025 he was a run-first starter: 487 rushing yards (3rd among QBs), a -0.19 CPOE, 6.7 yards per attempt, and a 36.5% pressure-to-sack rate that ranked 43rd of 62. This year his time to throw fell from 2.82 to 2.64 seconds, and he lived in the short and intermediate areas. He was 13 of 14 short and 8 of 11 between 10 and 19 yards, and he converted 8 of 9 third downs. All six designed runs were successful, and the rushing EPA held up at 0.335 a carry.

The numbers hide how small and soft the sample is. A league-best 0.578 EPA per dropback comes from 38 dropbacks, mostly against the worst defense in football. He went 7 for 7 with three touchdowns in the red zone, and no quarterback sustains that. The parts that look like his true self are less flattering. He went 0 for 3 on throws of 20+ air yards. One of his three pressures became a sack, in line with his rookie habit of holding the ball under duress. He also had a turnover-worthy fumble.

Where it goes from here depends on the depth chart, not on matchups. This offense leans run-heavy (pass rate 9.1 points under expected, 30th), and Winston is the starter. For now Dart is a stash with a promising single-game data point. He is not a weekly contributor.

strengths.title: Legs as a reliable floor
strengths.body: His designed runs went 6 for 6 in success at 8.2 yards a carry, which carries over the profile that made him the 3rd-best rushing QB by yards as a rookie. Rushing is the skill most likely to hold up whenever he plays again, because it held across both seasons.

strengths.title: Quicker, more accurate underneath game
strengths.body: He got the ball out faster than as a rookie and was close to perfect short and intermediate, with a 17-19 point CPOE in those zones. One game against the 32nd-ranked defense can't prove a jump in accuracy. Still, the faster release is a process change, and that kind of change tends to stick more than results do.

concerns.title: He isn't the starter
concerns.body: Winston has started Weeks 3 through 5, and Dart now sits fourth on the depth chart after a 12%-snap exit in Week 2 and a missed practice. Until that changes, none of his efficiency numbers turn into production.

concerns.title: Sample inflated by Dallas
concerns.body: Almost everything came against the defense that now ranks last in EPA, and 7-for-7 with three red-zone touchdowns is pure small-sample heat. His rookie baseline sits much closer to league average: 0.147 EPA a play and a negative CPOE.

concerns.title: Deep ball and sacks under pressure
concerns.body: He went 0 for 3 on deep throws. His pressure-to-sack rate stays high, matching a rookie year when he ranked near the bottom at turning pressure into sacks. That habit is part of a scrambler's trade, but his scrambles produced no first downs this year.

trend.note: He opened with a 26.6-point game against Dallas, left the Rams game after 12% of the snaps, and has since slid from starter to QB4 behind three straight Winston starts.

nextGame.headline: A soft Saints defense, but Dart likely won't see it
nextGame.body:
On paper New Orleans fits his game: 27th in defensive EPA, 31st against the run, and 28th against deep passes. A mobile quarterback could feast on that rush defense. Opponents also target tight ends against them at an above-league share, and Isaiah Likely was Dart's most efficient target. But Dart is QB4, so whatever this matchup offers goes to Winston.

On availability, the Saints are missing starting LB Kaden Elliss and two rotational DTs (Shepherd, Broughton), which further softens an already weak run defense. On the Giants side, RT Jermaine Eluemunor (90% of snaps) is questionable with a calf injury. That matters for any Giants quarterback, but for Dart it only becomes relevant if the depth chart changes.

keyMatchups.title: Porous Saints run defense
keyMatchups.body: New Orleans ranks 31st in run-defense EPA and 31st in defensive success rate, and it is short two DTs and its top linebacker. If Dart got any designed-run packages, this is the defense they would work against.

keyMatchups.title: Tight ends against New Orleans
keyMatchups.body: The Saints give up 0.66 EPA per target to the top tight end, 29th in the league, and see a bigger TE target share than the league norm. Whoever starts should lean on the middle of the field.

nextGame.watch: Whether Dart climbs back to QB2 or gets any snaps at all. That is the only thing that makes this matchup relevant to him.

restOfSeason.body:
The base case is that Dart doesn't start in the near term, since he is fourth on the depth chart behind a starter who has held the job for three weeks. If he gets back on the field, expect something close to his rookie form, not the Dallas game. That means meaningful rushing value, efficiency around league average as a passer, and a touchdown rate that settles well below 8.8%, all in an offense that passes far less than situations predict.

The faster release and the short-to-intermediate accuracy are the pieces worth watching for real growth. The 0.578 EPA per dropback and the perfect red-zone line will regress hard on any real sample. The projections below assume he starts, which is not the expectation.
swingFactors: Clarity on why Dart left Week 2 and missed practice

confidence.note: 38 dropbacks, mostly against the worst defense in football, and he is currently QB4 with no clear path to snaps.
